title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: PingOne
providers.scope_notes: Covers PingOne (PingOne Platform / Management APIs). SaaS; covers PingOne platform Worker apps and gateway credentials; inbound traffic policies need a Cloudflare-based custom domain.

controls.name: Application enable/disable toggle
controls.what: Disables a Worker app so it cannot be used.
controls.setting: Applications > Applications > (app) > toggle; API: PUT application enabled=false

controls.name: Refresh Token Duration
controls.what: Sets refresh token lifetime (default 30 days, 60 seconds to 1826 days).

controls.name: Inbound traffic policies
controls.what: Allow or block requests by CIDR and other verify rules, only on Cloudflare-based custom domains.

controls.name: Delete application
controls.what: Removes the Worker app and its secret (logged as APPLICATION.DELETED).

no_control.what: Access tokens for the PingOne API resource cannot be revoked via /as/revoke.

controls_unknown: Whether disabling the app or rotating the secret invalidates already-issued access tokens (role removal does take effect per call per S5)

authentication.summary: An interactive Worker app signs in an admin user through PingOne and gets an access token that carries that user's admin role assignments. The token calls the Management APIs as the user.

federation.details: User-delegated token; user sign-in may itself be federated to an external IdP.

ip_restriction.boundary: Same as pingone-1: inbound traffic policies only on Cloudflare custom domains; coverage of Management API calls not documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 60 min; refresh token 30 days default, up to 1826 days

renewal.expiry_basis: refreshTokenDuration on the app (rolling duration also configurable)
renewal.summary: If refresh tokens are enabled, new access tokens are minted without the user signing in again.

administration.summary: Access is bounded by the user's own role assignments, re-checked on each API call. Admins can disable the app, remove the user's roles, or shorten refresh token duration.
administration.conditions: Refresh tokens for custom resources can be revoked at /as/revoke; PingOne API resource tokens cannot.

sso.details: The token is issued after the user signs in through the authentication policies assigned on the Worker app's Policies tab.

inventory.details: GET /v1/environments/{envID}/applications lists the Worker apps, but not the user tokens issued through them.

sso.ui: Applications > Applications > [Worker app] > Policies > Pencil > select PingOne/DaVinci policies > Save

token_format.notes: RS256 JWT access token; refresh token may be opaque.

log_sources.name: PingOne Audit (Monitoring > Audit) and GET/POST /v1/environments/{envID}/activities
log_sources.notes: Configuration events kept 2 years, user events 90 days; queries max 14 days; Audit API rate 10/second.

log_sources.name: Subscriptions (webhooks)
log_sources.notes: Streams audit events to HTTPS/TCP endpoints; events lost if target down >7 days.

anomaly_cues: Admin actions from an unusual client app or IP
Long-lived refresh token use after the user left

containment.steps: Remove the user's admin roles, disable the app, or delete the user. Revoke refresh tokens at /as/revoke only applies to custom-resource tokens.
containment.notes: PingOne API access tokens cannot be revoked; roles are checked per call.

unknown: Sign-in event names for interactive worker apps were not checked
